sources.detail: The public API documents submittedDate range filtering, but that filters current indexed records by submission time; it does not by itself prove what collection state was publicly available at the exact knowledge horizon. Availability/indexing semantics remain unproven for BENCHMARK_CAPTURE_V0 PIT use.

The frozen source contract already authorizes cisagov/kev-data as a SAME_AUTHORITY_MIRROR. CISA documents that repository as its KEV data mirror and explicitly notes git commit history for tracking historical changes. A comparator can select the latest mirror commit not later than the knowledge horizon and bind the exact file blob/commit identity without consuming post-horizon state.

GDELT DOC supports STARTDATETIME/ENDDATETIME publication-time filtering, but the reviewed documentation does not establish an index-state or ingestion-time as-of boundary. A later query could therefore discover an article ingested after the horizon whose publication timestamp predates it. Exact collection-state PIT safety is unproven.

The frozen lane is a mutable repository search ordered by current updated state. Date qualifiers can restrict repository metadata values but do not prove the exact historical search membership, topic/archive state, or ordering visible at the knowledge horizon. No source-native historical result-set state is established.

The reviewed Hub API exposes current model listing/filter/sort metadata including lastModified, but no documented historical collection-state/as-of query for the global recently-updated model list. Filtering current metadata by timestamps would not establish exact horizon membership.

The official HN API exposes live top/new/best story lists and live change notifications, while the frozen lane uses the current front-page RSS collection. The reviewed public interface does not provide a historical front-page membership/ranking query for an arbitrary exact knowledge horizon.

PyPI documents the Latest Updates RSS feed as the latest newly created releases. The reviewed feed/API documentation does not establish a historical/as-of representation of that global feed collection for an arbitrary exact knowledge horizon.
